publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Electronic and optical methods of shaping wall antenna direction-finding characteristics have been presented. Advantages and disadvantages of each method have been described, with particular attention paid to weight systems being of key significance for beam forming process. It has been proved that in case of digital beam forming, the calculated weight values must be approximated following the spit of the applied phase shifters and mufflers. The authors conclude that the method selection depends upon antenna array components number (beam width). It is preferred to apply optical method for very narrow antenna beams.

articleTitle: 2-GHz 10-W power amplifier using combline resonators as the input and output matching sections
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The paper describes the design and development of a 1950-2150 MHz 10 W amplifier using combline resonators for impedance matching networks at the input and output ports. The design was initially simulated using Microwave Office v.2002 software, from Applied Wave Research Inc., indicating its feasibility. A commercial power FET was used for the amplifier. Experimental results obtained indicate that the amplifier is stable, has good input and output matching that result in the input and output return loss greater than 20 dB. The output power achieved is about 10 W.

articleTitle: Ground penetrating radar for sub-service detection (GPR-SSD)
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The paper describes a prototype radar, the "ground penetrating radar for sub-service detection" (GPR-SSD), realized in a V framework EU project. GPR-SSD has been designed from G.P.Tecno S.r.l. (Italy) in order to realize a reliable and low-cost apparatus able to detect sub-services (electrical cables, metallic and non-metallic pipes, i.e. gas pipes, etc.) without the need of skilled operators.

articleTitle: Wave propagation in random urban areas based on percolation paradigm
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: A computer model of wave propagation in random two-dimensional urban areas using the high-frequency ray-tracing method is presented. The randomness of the approach is realised by introducing a percolation model of the environment and model of ray arrivals based on the nonuniform Poisson distribution function. Computer simulation enables us to assign an approximate formula for magnitude of electric-field strength, which can be treated as an envelope of radio channel pulse response.

articleTitle: Teaching monolithic microwave integrated circuits design at the Faculty of Electronics and Information Technology, The Warsaw University of Technology
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: This paper describes a course on monolithic microwave integrated circuit design. The course is addressed to graduate and PhD students of the Faculty of Electronics and Information Technology, Warsaw University of Technology, Warsaw, Poland. It is entitled monolithic microwave integrated circuits. The course is 30 h of lectures + 15 h of laboratory experiments long.

articleTitle: Nonlinear frequency-selective device on magnetostatic waves
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Experimental investigation results of the suppression of various power level signals passing through a "microstrip resonator-ferromagnetic film" system in the case of magnetostatic backward volume wave excitation are demonstrated. A model is presented describing the nonlinear characteristics of such a device in the form of two coupled oscillatory circuits whose parameters depend on the input signal power levels. The nonlinear characteristics of the investigated device were obtained by simulation and are compared with experimental values.

articleTitle: E-book for "Fundamentals of Microwaves"
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The paper offers a description of a new model of academic book on "Fundamentals of Microwaves" based on modern multimedia tools. The new model was specially designed for the distance studies via the Internet offered by the Warsaw University of Technology. A detailed description of a universal structure of a textbook (e-book) is followed by the description of the tree-model of a lecture both from the technical and functional perspective.

articleTitle: Nonstationary excitation theory, integral and integral-differential equations for electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The Vainstain's theory for excitation of resonator and waveguides have been generalized for strong nonstationary case including nonlinear media and boundary conditions. The space-time tensor Green's functions and corresponding integral or integral-differential equations for linear and nonlinear media and inclusions have been constructed. The theory also generalized for waveguide transformers. The numerical results for pulse radiation by dipole currents and its propagation in resonators, waveguides and its discontinuities are presented.

articleTitle: FEM-based evaluation of manufacturing tolerances on a millimeter-waves rectangular to coplanar waveguide transition
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Rectangular to coplanar waveguide hermetic transitions are frequently used in satellite payloads, to interconnect rectangular waveguides toward antennas with internal active circuits, often realized in MMIC technology. The effects of manufacturing tolerances on this kind of transition are analyzed both in qualitative terms and in quantitative ones using a Monte Carlo method applied to FEM electromagnetic simulations. Results are compared with measures on a W-band prototype.

articleTitle: 700 MHz Split post dielectric resonator for measurements of the complex permittivity of fluoropolymer materials
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The split post dielectric resonator (SPDR) operating at frequency 700 MHz has been used to measure dielectric constant and loss tangent of fluoro-polymer materials. It has been proven that this technique allows one to measure real permittivity with uncertainty less than 0.5% and dielectric loss tangent with resolution on the order of 3/spl times/10/sup -5/ for low permittivity polymers.

articleTitle: Multifrequency microwave probing of nonlinear targets
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Numerical simulations of the process of nonlinear scattering of powerful microwave pulses by targets, which include semiconductor components, have been done. An attention is given to an incidence of several short probing pulses at different carrier frequencies. Numerical simulations are based on integral equations for induced current. A possibility to use multifrequency nonlinear scattering with releasing both sum frequency and difference one has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: An evaluation of synchronization influence on interference in TD-CDMA sytems
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The TD-CDMA technique is one of the modes assumed to use in 3G UMTS networks. The synchronization error influence on the interference level is discussed for TD-CDMA mode. The simulation model for method validation is described as well as the simulation results are also presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Possibility of reducing the number of channels in phase-antenna array
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: An analysis of an array antenna with a reduced number of elements (thin antenna) is presented. The paper concentrates on the antenna with an electronically scanned beam realized by phase shifters, but the results of the analysis and the conclusions are also true for fixed beam antennas. The problem concerns antennas with a reduced number of radiating elements without reducing the aperture size, and antennas with a reduced number of beamforming network channels without reducing the number of radiating elements (semi-thin antennas).

articleTitle: Calibration of full-polarization radar
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: A novel method of external calibration for polarization radar is proposed for accurate estimation of the backscattering matrix of radar objects. By using the reciprocity theorem for backscattering from a known reflector the calibration procedure can be simplified, the influence of background reflectors decreased and the requirements of passive reference reflectors lowered.

articleTitle: Reduction of microwave loss by use of laminated electrodes
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The use of thin film layered electrodes allows the unloaded Q-factor of a resonator to be enhanced due to resonant transmission of microwave power through metal sublayers. Use of superconducting films as the conductor plates needs additional analysis to establish the validity of applying the multilayer electrode consideration in this case. The method proposed is applied to the modeling of parallel plate resonators with maximum Q-factor.

articleTitle: Analytical and numerical simulation of artificial magnetic media realized by LTCC technology
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The goal of this work is analytical and numerical simulation of artificial magnetic medium (AM) realized by the LTCC technology. Simple analytical model based on periodically loaded transmission line presentation of AM is described. The simulated frequency response of AM slab and magnetic field distribution is presented. Real and imaginary parts of refractive index of AM slab were extracted from simulated data for AM slab with different number of unit cells. Designed AM exhibits good characteristics and can be used in microwave modules based on LTCC technology.

articleTitle: Wideband smart antenna using non-uniform components
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The benefits of using smart antennas to improve the performance of narrowband wireless communication systems have already been demonstrated by many researchers. In this paper, an investigation is performed into a wideband smart antenna, which is envisaged for applications in the next generation of wideband wireless communication systems. In order to simplify the design of such an antenna system, we propose new phased array architecture. It is assumed that such an array is formed by sets of antennas with beamforming networks, each serving only a narrow frequency sub-band. By choosing a suitable number of such antenna sets the array operates over a desired wide frequency band. Computer simulations of this antenna system are performed by neglecting mutual coupling effects and frequency dependence of elements forming each array set. The obtained results show that the system can successfully form beams to the desired direction in a wide frequency band.

articleTitle: New type of small broad-band internal antenna for third generation mobile phone handsets
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The paper presents a novel broad-band patch antenna for third generation mobile phone handsets. The planar U-shaped structure in configuration of the inverted-F antenna is reported. The characteristics of the radiating structure have been simulated using method of moments code and validated with measurements of the fabricated prototype. The bandwidth (VSWR of 2:1) of about 24,16%, covering PCS, DCS systems and uplink and downlink bands of the UMTS standard is obtained. Stable radiation patterns are observed across the passbands.

articleTitle: Technique of ultra wideband radar target discrimination using natural frequencies
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: An aspect independent radar target discrimination method based on the natural frequencies of ultra wideband radar targets is introduced. The sets of points in a multi-dimensional space corresponding to the poles on a complex plane (natural resonances) were offered as signatures of radar targets. This approach allows performing the automated discrimination algorithm of radar targets. The results of experimental research of the signals scattered by scaled aircraft models using the signatures algorithm and cumulant preprocessing are presented.

articleTitle: 3D macromodels in the FDTD filter analysis
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: This paper shows an application of 3D macromodels to filter analysis by means of the FDTD method macromodels are created using 3D FDFD description of the volume where singularities occur during a filter analysis. State equations are then used to form a second order system, which is reduced using ENOR algorithm. Reduced system (a macromodel) captures the singularity frequency behavior using a limited number of variables and is incorporated into the finite difference time domain routine as an iterative leap-frog scheme. Unlike subgridding this approach gives a high spatial resolution at a cost slightly shorter time step. Moreover, it allows one to analyze filters having strong field singularities accurately at the numerical cost comparable to that of the standard FDTD scheme.

articleTitle: Examples of usefulness of virtual receiving polarizations in radar
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Following a short sketch of the theory, numerical examples have been presented indicating the possibility of applying the concept of virtual receiving polarizations as the next step toward better clutter suppression in comparison with that using the OPCE methods employing reciprocal antennas.

articleTitle: Ultra wide-band transmissions: comparison of the impulse responses of two systems
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The present paper first resumes the general architecture of an ultra wide-band transceiver system. Two different system architectures are then studied and compared : the first of these terms an approbated Gaussian pulse; the second utilises a quasisinusoidal pulse. A comparison between the two, in terms of the power spectral density, the ease of signal generation, leads to the conclusion that the latter form offers a more advantageous solution.

articleTitle: Modelling of the millimeter magnetron performances
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The results of the theoretical investigation of millimeter magnetrons were described. The computational characteristics were compared with experimental ones. These results allowed us to estimate the performance of manufacturing devices. We calculated such as efficiency and current voltage via geometrical parameters.

articleTitle: Nonlinear dielectrics for tunable microwave components
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Agile materials and technologies based on nonlinear dielectrics like ferroelectrics or liquid crystals offer a line of passive tunable microwave components such as varactors, filters and phase shifters, suitable as key components in phased-array antennas e.g. for automotive radar sensors and in future reconfigurable (frequency-agile) RF-frontends, e.g. in mobile communication systems with multiband operation. The trend towards these commercial microwave applications involves a demand for cheaply integrated, compact devices with both, high tunability and low insertion loss. Therefore, distinct research interests have been focused on agile materials for tunable microwave components as promising alternatives to active semiconductor devices or MEMS varactors. Starting with some results of ferroelectric thin-film devices from literature, the focus of this paper will be on our research of tunable microwave components based on (1) ferroelectric thick-films on Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/-substrate and (2) liquid-crystals. Up to now, only very few approaches used an anisotropy at microwaves, e.g. for phase shifting purposes. However, with recently developed, novel highly-anisotropic microwave LCs, a figure-of-merit of above 110/spl deg//dB at 24 GHz has been achieved for a inverted-microstrip line phase shifter with comparatively low control voltages less than 30 V. At the same frequency, this exceeds by far the figure-of-merit of 30 to 50/spl deg//dB of BST-coplanar waveguide phase shifters, however, much lower tuning speed. This substantial progress opens up totally new low-cost LC applications beyond optics.

articleTitle: Metallized 3D foam technology: a well-suited solution for high performance, low-cost, CM-wave and MM-wave system integration
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The future emergence of high performance, low-cost microwave systems requires the development of well-suited technological solutions. A simple one is based on the use of a very common foam material, in combination with, on one hand, accurate 3D modeling techniques and, on the other hand, suitable metallization solutions, resulting in cost-effective high volume production abilities. By applying this foam technology, a wide range of microwave engineering issues can be successfully solved, both at centimeter-wave and millimeter-wave frequency bands. In this paper, the basics of the metallized 3D foam technology will be first described. Then, a primary experimental validation of this technology will be demonstrated by the fabrication of a few conventional devices, integrated in planar or wave-guide technologies. Finally, several added value microwave structures will be presented to illustrate the high flexibility and the multiple advantages offered by this integration approach, for a wide range of applications (at frequency up to 80 GHz).

articleTitle: State of the art high-speed photodetectors for microwave photonics application
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The paper reviews the recent advances in high-speed photodetectors based on A/sup 3/B/sup 5/ compounds for microwave photonics application. The two main trends in the evolution of the high speed photodetectors like improving of the bandwidth-efficiency product and increasing of the saturation current are discussed. The main types of the high-speed photodetectors such as p-i-n photodiodes, avalanche photodiodes, Schottky photodiodes, metal-semiconductor-metal photodetectors, resonant-cavity-enhanced photodiodes, waveguide photodiodes, traveling-wave photodetectors, and velocity matched distributed photodetectors are considered.

articleTitle: CMOS MMICs for microwave and millimeter wave applications
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Recent results on MMIC based on a 90-nm CMOS process are presented. Linear and nonlinear models were developed for the transistors based on S-parameters, noise parameters, and power spectrum measurements. Based on EM-simulations, models for multilayer capacitances, MIM-capacitances, various transmission lines etc were also developed. Amplifiers, frequency mixers, and frequency multipliers were then designed, fabricated and characterized. Amplifiers with a gain of 6 and 3.5 dB per stage at 20 and 40 GHz respectively, were demonstrated as well as frequency multipliers from 20 to 40 GHz with 15.8 dB conversion loss, and 30 to 60 GHz multipliers with 15.3 dB conversion loss. Resistive mixers at 20, 40, and 60 GHz were also demonstrated with promising results.

articleTitle: Multi physics multi scale modeling of microwave circuits and systems hybridizing circuit, electromagnetic and thermal modeling
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Modeling of complex systems requires that a systematic approach be adopted for multi scale and multi physics modeling. The current state of physical modeling tools in the arena of microwave and electromagnetic model is considerably mature enabling discrete problems to be considered. The real need is for hybridization of discrete modeling systems to obtain a seamless simulation environment from atoms to systems. The paper explores a strategy for multi physics multi scale modeling of microwave circuits and systems. It presents a framework guiding research in the development of electromagnetic and microwave modeling tools.

articleTitle: Integrated circuits for high speed optoelectronics
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The paper presents an overview of existing solutions for integrated circuits used in high speed (10 Gb/s and above) optical telecommunication systems. Available technologies are assessed for their advantages and the usefulness for optical transceivers. Currently available products and mature processes are included and only a brief discussion of emerging solutions is presented. The bulk of the paper is devoted to transimpedance amplifiers and driver circuits.

articleTitle: Advances in computational electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The paper presents a selection of techniques that are currently being investigated at the Technical University of Gdansk and can be used to accelerate CAD of microwave circuits and the computation of high and low frequency electromagnetic fields. Techniques for creating surrogate CAD models and their application to automated design of band pass filters are discussed. Different strategies of electromagnetic field representation for mesh based and meshless methods are introduced and their efficiency illustrated on examples involving structures with complex geometries.

articleTitle: 70 years of PIT - history and today of the Telecommunications Research Institute
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The Telecommunications Research Institute (PIT), the largest research and development center in Poland, boasts a long history. This year we will be celebrating the 70th anniversary of our Institute's founding; last year saw the 50th jubilee of our activity in the country defense sector. The Telecommunications Research Institute's roots go straight back to the State Institute of Telecommunication established in 1934. The Institute has been divided and merged again a number of times; it served as a basis to open other centers and institutes. Nevertheless the majority of staff and tasks have evolved into what is represented by today's PIT. All these years have been bridged by the company logo of a rhombus with the PIT abbreviation written into it. The paper shows the history and the latest achievements of the Telecommunications Research Institute. The research interests of the Institute over the years include radio navigation systems, radar and microwave technology, and command and control systems.
