articleTitle: European Web-based course on microwave transistor power amplifiers for Ph.D students
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The aim of the article is to present a groundwork for a Web-based course on microwave transistor power amplifiers for postgraduate students from Poland and Italy. Among lecturers are professors of the Universita degli Studi di Roma Tor Vergata in Italy. What follow is a course description and its aims.

articleTitle: A microwave method for measurement of free charge carriers mobility in semiconductor structures
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The use of the scheme of coherent signals subtraction (the synchrosignal and the synchronized Gunn oscillator output signal) in the measurement of charge carriers mobility in semiconductor structures by means of the microwave magnetoresistance method has been proved theoretically and experimentally. In this paper, the possibility of increasing the sensitivity of the microwave magnetoresistance method in semiconductor structures is investigated.

articleTitle: Analysis of 2-D correlation properties of sea surface backscattered signal
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: New radar technology applications need more and more advanced signal processing algorithms. In order to design processing algorithms it is necessary to dispose sufficiently accurate signal model. In this paper the 2-D correlation properties of sea surface radar return are analysed. The data for the analysis are real registered radar signals. The results show the dependence of correlation coefficients and correlation distances on range. Some parameters of power spectral density are introduced and analysed too. The conclusions formulated can be useful for modelling, simulation and segmentation of 2-D radar signals (images).

articleTitle: An efficient procedure for calibration of scanning phased antennas by means of near field planar scanner
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The paper present an easy and efficient procedure for the calibration of scanning phased antennas by means of a near field planar scanner. The main steps of the procedure - modeling of the antenna architecture, near-field data transformation and phase error corrections - are described. Measurement results, obtained by the proposed procedure, are also presented. The paper concludes with some discussions about the practical application and accuracy of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Optical methods for microwave signal generation
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Methods for optical generation of microwave signals are presented along with their perspectives. The utilization of optical technology in microwave signal generation offers new features and improved performance: like wider tuning range, higher stability, lower noise, synchronization, etc. The optical signal generation has already many applications, and it is expanding rapidly.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of multilayer radome with anisotropic materials
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Insertion loss and return loss expressions are derived for a plane multilayer radome consisting of anisotropic materials at normal, parallel and circular polarization of the incident electromagnetic wave. Numerical optimization of three layer radome based on thin honeycomb core is demonstrated for a wide range of elevation angle /spl theta/ in the frequency range 5-15 GHz.

articleTitle: Lightweight low gain microstrip antennas for use in minisatellites
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The paper presents the progress of investigations on small lightweight low gain antennas (LGA) for use onboard minisatellites and microsatellites. The LGA primary task is to ensure low rate data exchange in downlink and uplink communication channels with possible omnidirectional coverage, irrespective of the orientation of the spacecraft.

articleTitle: Doppler radar: retrieval of information about turbulence in rain
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Weather formations are objects of radar detection, measurement and recognition. Doppler radars are used to obtain necessary information for weather forecasts and aviation safety. One of the most important is information about the turbulence intensity in clouds and precipitation that is contained in spectra of echo-signals. This paper deals with Doppler radar observation of rain. A new method of turbulence intensity retrieval is introduced, discussed and checked using measured data.

articleTitle: From airborne via drones to space-borne polarimetric-interferometric SAR environmental stress-change monitoring - comparative assessment of applications
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Very decisive progress was made in advancing fundamental POL-IN-SAR theory and algorithm development during the past decade. This was accomplished with the aid of airborne and shuttle platforms supporting single-to-multi-band multi-modal POL-SAR and also some POL-IN-SAR sensor systems, which are compared and assessed with the aim of establishing the hitherto not completed but required missions such as tomographic and holographic imaging. Because the operation of airborne test-beds is extremely expensive, aircraft platforms are not suited for routine monitoring missions which is better accomplished with the use of drones or UAVs. Such unmanned aerial vehicles were developed for defense applications, however lacking the sophistication of implementing advanced forefront POL-IN-SAR technology. This shortcoming is thoroughly-scrutinized resulting in the finding that we do now need to develop the most rapid POL-IN-SAR drone-platform technology especially for environmental stress-change monitoring with a great variance of applications beginning with flood, bush/forest-fire to tectonic-stress (earth-quake to volcanic eruptions) for real-short-time hazard mitigation. However, for routine global monitoring purposes of the terrestrial covers neither airborne sensor implementation - aircraft and/or drones - are sufficient; and therefore multi-modal and multi-band space-borne POL-IN-SAR space-shuttle and satellite sensor technology needs to be further advanced at a much more rapid phase. The existing ENVISAT with the forthcoming ALOS-PALSAR, RADARSAT-2, and the TERRASAT are compared, demonstrating that at this phase of development the fully polarimetric and polarimetric-interferometric modes of operation must be viewed and treated as preliminary algorithm verification support modes and at this phase of development, they are still not to be viewed as routine modes.

articleTitle: Hybrid analysis of microwave components in cylindrical coordinates with function expansion in subdomains
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: A hybrid technique combining the discrete partial eigenfunction expansion (PEE) algorithm with 3D FDTD analysis m cylindrical coordinates is presented. The new technique is applicable to structures that have to be analyzed using a full 3D formulation but can also be divided into axial symmetric and not symmetric regions. Efficiency of PEE and versatility of 3D formulation are combined, and significant increase in efficiency, in terms of reduction of size of the problem and shorter simulation time is achieved.

articleTitle: Network-parameter-based modeling in microwave design
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: As system integration evolves and clock frequencies rise, it becomes increasingly important to consider the electrical behavior of previously neglected non-ideal effects of the microwave structures and components. This paper addresses the generation of broadband SPICE-based circuit models from frequency-domain network-parameters. A combination of subspace identification algorithm and vector fitting is applied to generate passive multi-port models of microwave devices characterized by measured or simulated network parameters. Results of the proposed method applied to microwave devices are given.

articleTitle: Efficient multimode mixed time-frequency domain analysis and optimization of waveguide structures
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Application of full-wave analysis and optimization method of waveguide structures having any desired topology is presented. Modeling of waveguide discontinuities by generalized scattering matrices are efficiently performed utilizing the modified FDTD-IBC method. Numerical optimization and model measurements of the 7-th order waveguide direct coupled cavity filter validate presented approach.

articleTitle: System power budget analysis of microwave radio links in Adana region
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: In this work, numerical analysis of system power budget is performed for radio link network design and transmission planning purposes; measured and calculated results are compared in order to analyse microwave radio link performance in Adana region under different conditions. Received power levels are measured, calculated and reported for different radio link types and environmental conditions. A new program is developed in order to make system power budget analysis. Measured and calculated results are compared, and the reasons of possible differences between them are investigated and interrogated.

articleTitle: "Microwave memory effect" of activated water and aqueous KOH solution
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: A "microwave memory effect" of the microwave activation of water and aqueous fluids has been discovered and studied. It has been found that microwave irradiation caused significant changes of the water structure in comparison to non-irradiated. The outline of the mechanism of the observed effect has been discussed. It has been assumed that microwave irradiation broke the hydrogen bond in a cluster-like water structure. As an effect, free water molecules, as well as hydroxyl ions, are generated. The technical application of the described effect - a new method of fast wet orientation dependent etching of silicon - has been studied. The potential dangerous consequences of the "microwave memory effect" have been discussed as well as technical applications in chemistry and microsystems techniques.

articleTitle: An equivalent lumped circuit describing magnetized plasma and its application in FD-TD modeling
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The paper describes a new approach to electromagnetic analysis of magnetized plasma using finite difference time domain (FDTD) method. An equivalent lumped circuit describing an FDTD cell filled with plasma is developed and applied in the analysis. Such a method is proved more effective than previously reported methods. The new approach is verified on a canonical example of known analytical solution.

articleTitle: Dielectric based frequency agile microwave devices
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Low loss highly tunable microwave material can be fabricated using dielectric laminate structure in which effective dielectric constant /spl epsiv//sub ef/ is efficiently controlled. The proposed combined structure usually consists of two dielectric parts with an air gap between them. This gap has to be arranged in such a way that provides the largest perturbation in the electromagnetic filed. By means of fast piezo electric mini-actuator, the size of the air gap is changed. As a result, the /spl epsiv//sub ef/ of given structure strongly varies that is used for device control. Wideband low loss waveguide phase shifters, highly tunable dielectric resonators, and based on them 20%-tunable filter are realized experimentally.

articleTitle: Anisotropy and local inhomogeneity of dielectric parameters of laminated substrates used for large-size RF-plates
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Two problems concerning laminated RF plates are considered - the anisotropy and local inhomogeneity of their dielectric parameters. Three resonance methods are used for the measurement of the longitudinal, transverse and equivalent (in microstrip configuration) dielectric constant and loss tangent. A large number of samples has been extracted from controlled areas in large-size plates of materials such as NH9338, RO4003, etc. The influence of standard deviations of these parameters on microstrip impedance, effective dielectric constant, phase delay, attenuation, etc. is estimated for design purposes.

articleTitle: Efficient wideband analysis of electromagnetic scattering and radiation problems
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: In this paper, single point and two point asymptotic waveform evaluation (AWE) are outlined as the efficient techniques for obtaining broadband response of wire radiators/scatterers from the method-of-moments (MoM) samples generated for a few isolated frequencies. An adaptive scheme, based on two-point AWE technique, is suggested for optimal choice of the location of the expansion points. Sample numerical results for two practical structures are given. The approach presented in the paper gives good accuracy and speed-up ratio for wideband analysis.

articleTitle: Quasi-elliptic two pole microstrip filter
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: A two pole microstrip bandpass filter which has two finite symmetrical transmission zeros is presented. To make extra transmission zeros, a source-load coupling is used. The filter has a center frequency of 3.3 GHz and a fractional bandwidth of 6%. The measured insertion loss is less than 0.35 dB in the bandpass.

articleTitle: Simplified description of the characteristics of microstrip resonators with a ferrite component
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Relatively simple approximate formulas are proposed for describing the transmission characteristics of HTS (high temperature superconductor) microstrip resonator structures with a monocrystalline ferrite component and for describing the microwave losses in such structures caused by magnetostatic waves. It is shown that excitation of magnetostatic waves leads to a decrease of the quality factor and to a "distortion" of the transmission characteristics of the structure.

articleTitle: Oblique plane wave scattering by an array of dielectric and metamaterial cylinders
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The influence of negative permittivity and permeability on the scattering patterns for dielectric and metamaterial posts is presented. Combination of an extended iterative scattering procedure and the orthogonal expansion method is used to investigate oblique scattering of an electromagnetic plane wave from an arbitrary configuration of parallel circular cylinders.

articleTitle: Bandpass filters with single transmission zeros at finite frequencies for adjusting slopes of frequency response
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to present new possibilities of designing known microstrip band-pass filters with one or two independent transmission zeros located in the stop-band far or close to the passband. A method of independently adjusting the slopes of the filter frequency response by proper placing transmission zeros is proposed. Each zero can he tuned to reject unwanted signals in the frequency range out of the passband. The transfer function of this type of filter is analytically expressed. The behaviour of a simple third-order lossless open-loop resonator filter is presented. The experimental results obtained for a third-order filter with a fractional bandwidth of 6 % at 2.4 GHz and six-order filter with a fractional bandwidth of 7% at 1.8 GHz are in a good agreement with the theoretical ones. The excellent performance and advantages of this class of filter have been presented.

articleTitle: Artificial neural networks modeling for computer-aided design of planar band-rejection filter
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Artificial neural networks (ANN) have recently gained attention as a fast and flexible vehicle to microwave modeling, simulation and optimization. This work presents an example of ANN usefulness in microwave filter (band-reject) design process, especially when the equivalent model of custom structure of the filter is unknown. A comparison of results from different simulation methods and measurements has been presented.

articleTitle: Application of optical dispersion techniques in phased array antenna beam steering
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Active phased array antennas play an important role in modern radar systems. This kind of antenna technique is a flexible way to apply electronic beam scanning in a wide angle range without the need for mechanical rotation of the antenna and easy spatial beam shaping, achieved by independent control of the transmitting elements. The paper describes the concept of an optoelectronic components application for the construction of a system targeted at steering a 16 element linear antenna. The concept of the steering system applies the dispersion phenomenon in single-mode optical fibres to obtain a tuned time delay of the microwave signals applied to the antenna elements. Very high resolution and an excellent accuracy of the antenna beam positioning have been achieved.

articleTitle: A new low-noise amplifier topology to rival conventional designs
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: A novel current-mode BiCMOS low-noise amplifier is compared to conventional voltage-mode topologies, emphasising on performance at 900 MHz. Rivalling classical designs in performance, this new design has the added advantage of controllable gain. Comparisons in terms of the major parameters: gain, noise figure, power consumption, signal quality: reveal that this new approach provides excellent possibilities.

articleTitle: Integral equation analysis of shielded dielectric resonators
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The method of analysis of shielded dielectric resonators characterized by rotational symmetry is presented. The formulation is based on coupled volume and surface integral equations (VIE/SIE) and enables characterization of inhomogeneous structures. The equations are solved numerically by the method-of-moments (MoM) computational scheme. The example calculation results for axially symmetric TE modes are given.

articleTitle: Strongly nonlinear feedback technique for significant phase noise suppression at microwave harmonic oscillators
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Calculations are presented to study the phase noise suppression effects of an additionally introduced highly nonlinear feedback loop in microwave harmonic oscillators. Calculations are done for determining the optimal structure and parameter set of nonlinearly feedbacked harmonic oscillators, with respect to the effects of the nonlinear properties on the behaviour of the phase noise characteristics. Using the calculated analytical form /spl sim/6 dB of phase noise suppression was achieved. Measurement and simulation results far confirming our theoretical principles are also reported.

articleTitle: Bandwidth enhancement of a transmit array-type spatial power combiner with the use of stacked patches
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The use of stacked patch (SP) antennas is proposed for enhancing an operational bandwidth of a spatial power combiner employing a planar amplifying transmit array (TXA). In this array, input and output ports of individual amplifiers are equipped with orthogonally oriented SP antennas, which are located on opposite sides of the ground plane. A 4 /spl times/ 4 SP TXA, along with two hard horns, is designed and constructed to form an X-band spatial power combiner. This device is experimentally tested showing an increased operational bandwidth in comparison with its counterpart that uses edge-feed microstrip patch antennas.

articleTitle: All-optical intensity noise suppression of solid-state lasers for optical generation of microwaves
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: This paper reports on a new all-optical technique of relative intensity noise suppression for solid-state lasers. The new scheme we have used is based on an unbalanced fiber interferometer (UMZ) which is able to cancel the intensity noise peak at relaxation oscillations.

articleTitle: Modelling and simulation of urban multipath propagation
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: A Suzuki distribution has proved useful for modelling fading-shadowing channels of urban multipath propagation. The Suzuki model, which has a complicated integral form, is accurately described. A method of generating Suzuki distributed random sequence is proposed. The results can be used for simulation experiments in order to avoid costly hardware tests of wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Trends in radar technology and PIT achievements
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: General trends observed in development of radar technology has been marked and today's status of Polish radar development and its trends is given in the paper. The influence of access of modern technologies on Polish radar design is also presented. A brief description of a new generation of 3D long radar L and S-band coherent surveillance radar are given. A mobile medium range S-band radar is presented. The ELINT/ESM systems on armored vehicles are described. Transmit-receive modules developed in PIT in L, S and C frequency band are described and their influence on future red systems developed in Poland.

articleTitle: A wide-band double-PLL microwave frequency synthesizer
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: We describe a wideband microwave frequency synthesizer operating from 2 to 18 GHz. The synthesizer is based on a YIG-tuned oscillator (YTO), a sampling phase detector (SPD) working as a sub-harmonically pumped mixer and a double PLL integrated circuit for stabilizing the frequencies of a local oscillator and the YTO. The whole circuitry is supervised by a microcontroller. For this design, we discuss the underlying issues that regard flexible frequency control and optimization of the phase noise performance.

articleTitle: Modeling of noncoordinate plane waveguide exciter structure for 2-D analysis by finite element method
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: For investigation of plane waveguide structures circle sector finite element is proposed. Finite element of that form fulfils rand current conditions. Analytical expressions for orthogonal surface currents on such element are given. Properties of sector finite element are from element bent in waveguide cross section dependent. Use the sector finite element a noncoordinate waveguide exciter is investigated.

articleTitle: Ultra broadband transmission line transformers - planar realization principles
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Three Guanella-type transmission line transformers (TLT) are presented: a coiled TLT on a GaAs substrate, a straight ferriteless TLT on a multilayer PCB and a straight hybrid TLT that employs semi-rigid coaxial cables and a ferrite. All three devices have 4:1 impedance transformation ratio, matching 12.5 /spl Omega/ to 50 /spl Omega/. Extremely broadband operation is achieved. A detailed description of the devices and their operational principle is given. General aspects of the design of TLT are discussed.

articleTitle: Advances in RF-microwave and light sources for applications in therapeutic medicine
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The expansion in the use of RF/Microwaves and optical sources in therapeutic medicine is dramatic. In this paper, some of the ongoing therapeutic modalities will be mentioned with the emphasis on our future research, for example: our attempts to combine microwaves and laser sources in therapeutic medicine, such as their applications in photodynamic therapy, and the utilization of blue LED's (light emitting diodes) for neonatal phototherapy.

articleTitle: Optimization of a very low-size, planar UMTS duplexer, using new miniaturized open-loop resonator filters
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: An optimized topology of planar UMTS duplexer has been developed in this work. This circuit is based on both the use of novel ultra-compact open-loop resonator filters and a well-suited T/sub x/ and R/sub x/ filter combination. With this solution, all the required specifications for a high-level, low-cost integration have been encountered. The design methodology of the new miniaturized filters and the description of the filters combination into a very low-size duplexer configuration are successively given. Finally, measurements for a UMTS device are presented.

articleTitle: Si-Ge power amplifier for WCDMA handheld applications
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: A monolithic radiofrequency power amplifier for WCDMA handheld applications has been fabricated in a 0.35 /spl mu/m, 40 GHz f/sub T/, volume production Si-Ge bipolar technology. The process technology features a doped ground connection for on-chip devices to improve the overall performance. At 3.3 V supply voltage saturated output power of 29 dBm with a PAE of 50 % has been achieved; simultaneously P/sub -1dB/ is 28 dBm at 1.95 GHz and the small signal gain is 32 dB.

articleTitle: Control and diagnostic unit of X-band radar transmitter
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The functional description, design and performance of a quad-microprocessor module, provided for controlling the X-band radar transmitter with a travelling wave tube are presented in detail.

articleTitle: An accurate fast-algorithm for analyzing and optimizing cylindrically stratified radomes
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: An accurate and fast algorithm to analyze and optimize cylindrically stratified radomes; is presented. A key point in the algorithm is the calculation of Green's function. A spectral-domain approach connected with a generalized transmission line model (GTLM) is used. Using this model an asymptotic approximation to perform a fast far field calculation is given. Based on far field approximation a wide-range frequency optimization of the radome is also given.

articleTitle: Wide band combline filters
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: A new accurate method for design of wide band combline filters is presented. The method is based on a new concept of center frequency of coupled combline resonators. The design example of a filter having 54% bandwidth is presented. The measurements show an excellent agreement with theory.

articleTitle: Microwave synthesizer with frequency multiplying module
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The paper describes a synthesis approach that employs a multiplied phase locked source that generates RF signals from 500 MHz to 18 GHz in 1 MHz steps.

articleTitle: Environment influence on the array antenna radiation pattern in the far zone
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The paper presents the environment influence on the antenna radiation pattern. The zoning (the near and the far zones) wax analyzed. The parameters of antenna and the background were considered. The numerical results were simulated on the basis of theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Monopulse microstrip antenna on 2.4 GHz
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: A monopulse antenna prepared in microstrip technology is presented in this work. A model antenna construction is shown and different variants of beamforming circuits with differential canals in two planes are discussed. Results of measurements of the antenna model are presented.

articleTitle: Resonant frequencies of helical resonators
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The paper investigates the resonant frequencies of helical resonators. Full-wave 3D electromagnetic analysis is used to verify closed-form formulas known from literature. Corrections to formulas for dominant mode and new formulas for higher modes are proposed. Two-helical resonators filter was designed and measured.

articleTitle: Analysis of the mutual impedance of two linear dipoles as function of their height above the ground surface
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: In the paper the applicability of a system, consisting of two linear dipoles located above the surface of a layered half-space for measuring the dielectric characteristics of soils is discussed. Measurement results of the real part and module of the active antenna's full impedance as function of humidity (uniformly distributed along the surface and in depth) are presented for the sandy soil case. The experiments are compared with calculations.

articleTitle: The computation of electrical fields on a heart model with a microwave catheter
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: In our paper, we calculated the distribution of an electric field modulus at several parallel cross-sections of a model heart (with a catheter inside of its right atrium). The catheter was created out of dielectric or metal material. The frequency of the microwave signal was f = 10 GHz. The distribution of the electric field modulus has resonance peaks. The electric field could be concentrated in different places of the heart depending on weather the material of the catheter was dielectric or metal.

articleTitle: Wide-band analysis of highly resonant wire antennas and scatterers via adaptive sampling
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Efficient wideband evaluation of antennas and scatterers is essential for solving many electromagnetic engineering problems. Deriving the samples of the required parameter from frequency-domain computations at uniform intervals becomes prohibitively computationally expensive for highly resonant structures. A dynamic adaptive frequency sampling technique partially overcomes this difficulty. In this paper, the features of the technique applied in combination with method-of-moments to a variety of highly resonant wire antennas and scatterers are investigated.

articleTitle: Smart antenna technology for high-altitude-platform based wireless communication systems
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: We present a digital beamforming scheme for future wireless communication systems based on high altitude platforms. The proposed digital beamforming scheme, which is installed on the platforms in high-altitude-platform (HAP) systems, can reduce significantly the number of antenna elements and the corresponding receiver modules, analog to digital (A/D) converters etc. without loss of performance. As a result, the system complexity and system costs can be reduced, therefore, enhancing feasibility of HAP based systems. Furthermore, in the proposed scheme, we can specify narrow main beamwidth and low sidelobe level simultaneously. Illustrative design examples and beam-pattern comparisons with traditional digital beamforming methods are included.

articleTitle: Improving accuracy of FDTD modelling in biological applications
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: This contribution demonstrates a possibility of improving accuracy of the continuous wave steady-state FDTD prediction of the EM field and the specific absorption rate (SAR) distributions in the layered biological tissues by reducing the numerical dispersion error via appropriate direct modification of the constitutive parameters of the tissues. The attractiveness of the approach lies in that the enhanced accuracy of the FDTD prediction is obtained at the negligible cost of a trivial pre-processing of the material parameters.

articleTitle: Polarization of a plane wave scattered by an array of cylinders
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The theory of TE- and TM-wave scattering by an array of conducting and dielectric cylinders is investigated using a combination of an iterative scattering procedure and the orthogonal expansion method. Polarization parameters of the scattered plane wave are derived in the near and the far fields.

articleTitle: X-band microwave surface mounted filters based on stripline with two layer asymmetric substrate
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: A design concept of a microwave filter structure is presented. This concept allows the filters to be fabricated as independent elements for surface-mounting in a microwave circuit PCB. The filter design is based on a stripline with a substrate made from two different layers. In addition, the design of a special metal housing is shown. The simulation and measurement results of the filter model are presented Filters fabricated according to this concept are very low-cost and insensitive to ambient conditions. They are designed to be used in the ARS-800 radar system.

articleTitle: Simulation study of mobility management procedures for IP-based wireless communications system
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: In this paper, simulation approach for verification and evaluation of the proposed mobility management mechanisms is presented. The architecture of considered wireless communications system consists of three main components, i.e. core communications segment (CCS), wireless local area networks (WLANs) and network management centre (NMC). The paper is based on both Home Agent (HA) replication and user's services profile transferring to a new location is described in detail. WLAN is connected to the core communications segment by high capacity line of sight (HCLOS) radio links. Network management center performs an essential role in supporting the mobility management functions. Both COMNET and OPNET simulation packages were used for quality assessment of the modified IPv6 mobility management procedures. The simulation results presented in the paper confirmed that the modified procedures significantly improve the wireless network accessibility.

articleTitle: Multielement linear array antenna for radar applications
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The paper presents the design and construction of the 48 elements linear array antenna. Radiating elements and the multipart power divider of the antenna have been constructed in an air triplate line technology. The theoretical and experimental results have been compared.

articleTitle: A communication system for scientific minisatellites
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: This paper shows technical issues relating to the telecommunication system of minisatellite design, and gives an example of transceiver design and technical requirements of space qualified transceivers. It also describes the implemented solutions in ESEO and SSETI Express minisatellites, which will be launched soon.

articleTitle: A switched-beam radial horn antenna design
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The design of an antenna consisting of a monopole circular array placed inside a radial waveguide is discussed. The main beam of the array can be steered around the azimuth plane by changing the reactive loads of the peripheral monopoles surrounding a central monopole. Housing this array in a radial guide with a suitable transition to free space results in an increased return loss bandwidth. An increased beam gain is also observed.

articleTitle: Integrodifferential model of artificial fractal medium
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: We consider the geometric and physical aspects that permit introduction of the so-called /spl alpha/-characteristics for studying the behavior of electromagnetic field components in the vicinity of a set of points with fractal properties. The model of charges and /spl alpha/-pole moments for study of spatial properties of plasmoids (the nonuniform fractal filling of some area by clots of the homogeneous plasma) is designed. The own functions and numbers of electromagnetic waves, which propagate in rectangular waveguide with fractal wide walls, have been determined using the apparatus of fractional integro-differential calculus.

articleTitle: Direct and inverse problems solutions for coaxial and waveguide probes
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The solutions of direct and inverse problems for coaxial and rectangular waveguide probe structures (CPS and WPS) with multilayered media are presented. The direct problems are formulated as the analysis of CPS and WPS using the integral equation method or stationary formulation of problems. It allows one to obtain fast algorithms for the direct problems. The inverse problems are the determination of slab parameters (permittivities, permeabilities, and thicknesses). The least square method and artificial neural networks (ANN) have been used to solve the inverse problems.

articleTitle: A novel wideband CDMA receiver
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: This work presents an even harmonic direct conversion receiver for WCDMA applications. The receiver uses a very low noise LNA to provide the gain and low noise requirements. A subharmonic pumping mixer converts the RF signal to the baseband signal. This cost effective mixer is well suited for DC offset and even harmonics suppression. In order to decrease the receiver size, some techniques such as reduced size branch line coupler and Wilkinson power divider with the lumped elements are used. The simulation results show that the specifications of proposed receiver fully satisfy the requirements of the WCDMA receiver.

articleTitle: Low noise terahertz receivers
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: This paper is reviewing recent work on low noise mixers and LO sources for THz frequencies. Progress on heterostructure barrier varactor triplers and quintuplers are briefly discussed. It is pointed out that quantum noise becomes significant at THz frequencies.

articleTitle: Conical and broadside radiation of a discrete spherical Luneburg lens fed by a conformal printed antenna
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The presented MAR technique is a very powerful and economic method to study the radiation problems for discrete Luneburg lens antennas (DLLA) integrated with conformal patch feed. It enables one to highlight with controlled accuracy all the key physical effects such as the patch-cavity and whispering-gallery resonances and the main beam collimation. This technique deals with a full field computation.

articleTitle: Geometric interpretation of the characteristic polarizations
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The scattering mechanism can be analyzed from the geometrical point of view using the polar decomposition which decomposes the normalized scattering matrix in a unitary matrix and in a Hermitian (positive definite) one. Each of them can be built using parameters (polar parameters) such as vectors, angles and scalars which have geometrical meaning in the Stokes space. In this work it is shown the relation between them and some of the characteristic polarizations of a normalized, symmetric scattering matrix: the copolar null and the copolar maxima. Moreover, the inverse relations are found: the parameters which characterize the unitary and the Hemitian matrices can be expressed as function of the copolar nulls only. Using these relations, the problem to find the polarizations such that the received voltage is maximized (or minimized) for a given S, is reduced to apply the polar decomposition and compute the polar parameters. Furthermore, the scattering matrix is parameterized by the characteristic polarization states. Since it exists a direct connection between a unitary matrix and a rotation and between a Hermitian matrix and a boost, the Mueller (or Kennaugh) matrix can be built using the same parameters. This is the first step towards the study of the characteristic polarization states in the more general case of received partially polarized waves, the stochastic case.

articleTitle: Modulation of the output power of semiconductor microwave oscillators by changing the voltage in bias circuit
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The use of the scheme of coherent signals subtraction (the synchrosignal and the synchronized oscillator output signal) for realization of the simple method of control of the output power of semiconductor microwave oscillators on the example of Gunn oscillator by the changing the bias of an active element has been proved theoretically and experimentally. The change up to 40 dB of the oscillator output power at the constant output frequency, when bias changes on 2.7%, has been achieved.

articleTitle: Modeling of composite materials on the basis of conducting fibres
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: A numerical technique for calculating the polarizability of thin-wire elements is presented. The calculations are based on the integral equation method. The computation of the polarizability of spiral particles is performed and the comparison of its results with data based on the theory of circuits is carried out. The Maxwell-Garnett approach is used for the calculation of effective constitutive parameters of an artificial chiral composite consisting of a dispersion of spiral particles in free space. The opportunity to control its parameters by varying the geometry of the particles is shown.

articleTitle: The investigation of DDL at fundamental and higher bands
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: A dispersive delay line (DDL) with a dispersive interdigital transducer (having variable spaced fingers) and with a simple periodic transducer is examined. The possibility to obtain higher band of the DDL in a case of its specific configuration being a nonperiodic electrodes structure of the dispersive transducer is described. Experimental results of the research for chosen parameters of the DDL at a fundamental and higher bands are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Doppler RAKE detection in fast-fading environment
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The conventional RAKE detection of the code division multiple access (CDMA) system exploits multi-path diversity, but is only optimal in slow- fading scenarios. For fast-fading environments, where Doppler effect has a significantly detrimental impact on detection, the Doppler-RAKE receiver, which jointly exploits time and frequency diversity, is being researched as one possible solution. We further develop the system in several aspects to ameliorate its performance, while considering the trade-offs between its improved effects and the increased complexity of the algorithms.

articleTitle: Wireless LAN IEEE 802.11b adaptation for military purposes
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: This paper describes possibilities of civilian WLAN adaptation for military purposes. The analysis contains both possible modifications of COTS equipment and construction of brand new solutions, based on existing VLSI integrated circuits. The main goal of each adaptation is utilization of military frequency bands and increase of output power.

articleTitle: Estimation of Doppler-polarimetric spectrum of signals reflected from distributed radar objects
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Polarization parameters and their Doppler spectrum of reflections characteristics coming from volumetric distributed radar objects are estimated for Doppler-polarimetric radar using complex modulations signal transmission the case of complex signals using. The influence of the sounding signal's ambiguity function on the possible joint estimation of the velocity spectra and separate backscattering matrix elements of objects is shown. Simulation results of our algorithms estimating the matrix Doppler spectrum are presented for the case of PCM and LFM transmissions.

articleTitle: Terahertz photonics for imaging
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: This paper concerns the application of microwave photonic techniques for Terahertz imaging. The system under investigation comprises of two high power, low noise electro-optic microchip lasers that mix in a traveling wave detector to produce a 200 GHz millimeter wave signal that is multiplied to .8 or 1.2 THz. The traveling wave detector, the multiplier and the THz radiating elements are to be integrated on an MMIC chip. The paper focuses on the development of the laser subsystem.

articleTitle: Methods of radiometric images improvement with regularization and prior information application
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: In this paper the radiometric images construction solution regularization methods under the application of prior information methods were analyzed. The regularization procedure influence on image spectra extrapolation was shown.

articleTitle: Dynamic characteristics of gain-coupled InGaAsP laser diodes and their reliability
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Dynamic characteristics of partly gain-coupled multiple-quantum-well InGaAsP distributed feedback laser diodes have been investigated. Basic dynamic parameters (differential gain, K-factor, differential carrier lifetime) were found out. It is shown that the increase of coupling coefficient results not only in both oscillation and damping frequency increasing, but also in time-resolved frequency chirp oscillation decreasing. Relation between K-factor and differential carrier lifetime and their correlation with deferential gain indicates essential differential gain role in dynamic parameter dispersion.

articleTitle: Wavelet based analysis of microstrip structures on triangular grids
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: In this paper novel wavelets based on Rao-Wilton-Glisson-functions are introduced for method of moments on triangular grids. To demonstrate matrix sparsity, they are applied to a generic microstrip example. The approach combines the flexibility of a general grid based on triangles with the data and CPU-time saving potentials of a wavelet expansion.

articleTitle: The performances of algorithm for flow management in up-link of CDMA networks
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The radio-resources management (RRM) in future CDMA networks is discussed taking into account the variety of services classes in 3G/4G systems. An optimising algorithm to control of data streams in up-link is described. The required signal-to-interference ratio is a criterion used in this algorithm. For this criterion, a method of interference estimation was elaborated and it is also discussed here. The simulation model for method validation is described as well as the simulation results are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: A 100W ISM-2.45GHz band power test system
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: This paper describes development of solid-state microwave power test system (MPTS) operating over 2.3 to 2.6 GHz with the output power level of 100 W for industrial applications in material processing, and for designing of microwave power industrial equipment. The MPTS unit consists of four major parts: PLL synthesizer, high power solid-state amplifier, detector probes for return losses and leakage measurement and microcontroller. The MPTS system is able to operate in either single fixed-frequency regime, or in swept mode with self-tuning for minimum reflection of a heated load.

articleTitle: Volume and integrated p-i-n modulators in millimeter frequency range
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The millimeter frequency range is being intensively investigated. Novel types of oscillators, both diode-like (TUNETT) and lasers have been put forward; the search of effective control devices is also of great interest. Volume and surface oriented integrated p-i-n-structures modulators have demonstrated high efficiency in millimeter wave range. These structures possess high modulation and high-speed properties, sustain great EM powers, but their modulation characteristics in millimeter and sub millimeter range have not been yet investigated in detail. A comparison and criteria of these modulators based on silicon, in millimeter range are presented here.

articleTitle: On the influence of mesh refinement and nonuniformity on the solution of the heat transfer equation in coupled EM-thermal analysis
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: A modelling tool for microwave power industry has to account for not only electromagnetic phenomena, but also the heat transfer effect. In this paper the numerical error analysis of the FDTD method employed to solve the heat transfer equation has been performed together with an investigation of the influence of mesh refinement on the solution. Analytical predictions have been verified with numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Analysis of microstrip structure on piezoelectric surface by means of singular integral equations
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The method of singular integral equations has been used to analyse the microstrip structure on piezoelectric surface. As physical example we computed the electric charge density on a metal strip at different time moments.

articleTitle: Active MMW microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Gunn diode oscillators coupled with a log-periodical microstrip antenna, were experimentally studied at frequencies 25-60 GHz. A microstrip antenna was mounted on a dielectric plate with a thickness of about a quarter of wavelength. The backside of the dielectric plate was metalized. Generated power was measured as 5 mW, that was more than 50% of maximum output power generated with the same diode, mounted into the metal waveguide cavity. The oscillation regime varied from single-mode to a noise-like one depending on the dielectric thickness and could be synchronized by an external signal. Such a quasi-optical performance of the Gunn-diode oscillator is feasible for power combining in the open resonator that is essentially promising for applications at millimetre waves.

articleTitle: Rotational seismic events recognition basing on fiber-optic Sagnac interferometer application
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The paper presents the idea as well as the results of a fiber-optic Sagnac interferometer application for recognition of rotational seismic events. The presented devices based on well-known optical gyroscope configuration is optimized for detection of other special physical quantities. Generally it is a rotational seismometer designed for calibration of the other electromechanical types of such devices, as well as a new sensor for detection of rotational seismic events. The detection of absolute rotation by the system is advantageous in comparison to the other rotational seismometers, which calculate rotational events in indirect ways.

articleTitle: Modeling of planar periodic antennas using Floquet's theorem by the method of lines
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: This work describes an efficient and accurate algorithm for modeling of planar periodic antennas. The proposed algorithm is based on the method of lines (MoL). It will be shown, that finite periodic antenna arrays can be modeled combining Floquet's theorem with impedance transformation. To take into account antenna's radiation, absorbing boundary conditions (ABC) are used. The proposed formulation is substantiated with numerical results of an eight-slot antenna-array.

articleTitle: Propagation in a ferrite cylindrical waveguide magnetized by a two four-pole magnetic fields
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The normal modes of a transversely magnetized ferrite cylindrical waveguide are found using a coupled mode approach. The bias yoke generates an electrically rotatable four-pole transverse magnetic field in the ferrite producing birefringence phase shift. The changes of polarization state of the electromagnetic wave at the output of the guide sections of different lengths are investigated and applied to develop a rotatable half-plate section useful for phase shifter design.

articleTitle: Green functions and integral equations for photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The Green functions and corresponding integral and integral-differential equations for periodic structures are introduced. Several results based on this approach for 1D, 2D, and 3D photonic crystals are presented.

articleTitle: Sierpinski monopole antenna-uniplanar feeding technique
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Various feeding techniques for Sierpinski fractal monopole antennas are considered. To find low profile uniplanar antenna construction a novel feeding technique has been proposed: coaxial-fed with extended ground plane and coplanar waveguide with finite dimensions of the ground plane. The measurements of the fabricated antennas prototypes confirm usefulness new feeding technique.

articleTitle: Asterism decoding for layered space-time systems
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The area of layered space-time (LST) systems has received enormous attention recently as they can provide a roughly linear increase in data rate by using multiple transmit and receive antennas. The optimal detection strategy for a LST receiver is to perform a maximum-likelihood (ML) search over all possible transmitted symbol combinations. The decoding scheme proposed in this paper, called Asterism decoding, looks for a more efficient way of finding the ML solution by first considering the case of multiple transmit antennas and a single receive antenna. The decoder is then extended to achieve ML like performance for any number of receive antennas. It is then shown that Asterism decoding has an approximate order of magnitude reduction in computational complexity when compared to ML decoding. Asterism decoding is the first lower complexity decoder that achieves ML-like performance for systems where the number of receive antennas is less than the number of transmit antennas without the additional use of error coding.

articleTitle: The influence of HEMT nonlinear distributed modeling on transient performance of microwave circuits
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: This paper presents the impact of electromagnetic wave propagation on HEMT device electrodes in transient response. The proposed model is used in analysis and simulation of a MMIC compatible, Ka band power amplifier. Final results are the comparison between the simulation results in semi-distributed and lumped models, respectively.

articleTitle: About capabilities of objects location using microwave radiometer
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Microwave thermal radiation of various objects can be used for their location and identification. Thermovision in the infrared range enables to find temperature distribution on the object surface while microwave radiometers allow to recognize hot objects placed for instance, behind thermal shields. In the paper the authors present selected results of the research on passive system for discovering live creatures based on microwave radiometer. Performed experiments showed that assumptions were correct and the radiometer is very useful for such applications.

articleTitle: Frequency and time simulation of electromagnetic field of microwave antenna array
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The paper presents a using of the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method for antenna arrays analysis for the mobile and stationary base stations of the radiocommunication systems. Theory base of the design of quadrate antenna array as a base element of complicated radiation structures is described; a steady phase excitation for this base array in broad frequency band is proposed. The results of computer simulation by FDTD method of frequency characteristics, the radiation patterns and near time electromagnetic field evolution of this array over finite ground plane are presented.

articleTitle: A BITE subsystem for phased array transmit antenna control
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: In the paper, a BITE subsystem to control radar antenna system parameters with transmit pulse power up to several hundreds KW is described. The proposed BITE subsystem is used to control parameters of the transmit beam forming network with 24 radiating structures. At the input of the transmit beam forming network the input pulse power is measured by a detector placed in the decoupled port of the directional coupler. At all outputs of the beam forming network, directional couplers with the same type of detectors are used to control the output power distribution. Output voltage from detectors are supplied to 8-bit microcontrollers with built-in A/C converter and information about amplitude distribution at the input of antenna rows and input VSWR of the antenna rows after final processing in the master microcontroller is supplied to the radar central computer. As a test signal the pulse power from the radar transmitter is used. Antenna parameters are controlled at nominal power level in on line mode of radar operation. Special attention is paid to the reduction of the cost of the BITE subsystem, low cost components are used and a new design of the low cost directional coupler is proposed.

articleTitle: Optical true time-delay feeder for phased array antennas using fiber Bragg gratings and metal film reflectors
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: We propose a novel optical true time-delay (TTD) feeder for phased array antennas (PAAs) using a fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) prism and Cr/Au film reflectors directly deposited on cleaved fiber ends. This structure requires less number of FBGs than the previously proposed FBG-only TTD feeders and also provides the flexibility in wavelength selection due to the uniform reflectance of the metal film in a broad wavelength range. A TTD feeder with two delay lines for 10 GHz linear PAAs capable of steering beams in three directions at 0/spl deg/ and /spl plusmn/30/spl deg/ has been built. Experimental results on time delays are in good agreement with those calculated at all the steering angles.

articleTitle: Visualization of leaky waves on planar transmission lines
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: This paper presents a visualization of leaky waves excited by delta-gap sources on planar transmission lines, namely the 2nd surface and space leaky modes on the slotline, and the dominant and surface leaky modes on the conductor-backed slotline. The field is modeled by numerical calculation in the time domain. The simulations show the character of the leaky waves excited by delta-gap sources and are a useful tool for the investigation of leaky waves.

articleTitle: Design of a point-to-point radio link receiver using software-radio
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Current narrowband point-to-point radio microwave link technology relies heavily on analog components for channel tuning and gain control. Although these systems provide a good performance, analog components drift with time necessitating frequent tuning throughout the lifetime of the equipment. This drawback can be significantly mitigated by adopting digital techniques to carry out the radio functions. This work presents the design of a digital software system to replace functions traditionally implemented using analog components and illustrates, through measurement results, the feasibility of the system.

articleTitle: 2,4/60 GHz converters for "last mile" technology
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Possibilities of 2,4 and 60 GHz wireless network design in application to "last mile" technology are studied on the basis of the standard 802.11b. In the lack of the standard on wireless networks in mm-wave range, the wireless hybrid network looks as feasible. Multibeam commutated antenna application and stabilization of mm-wave oscillators are considered as possible. In this work the loop of frequency converters "up" and "down" was experimentally investigated.

articleTitle: Investigation of high frequency modulation of InGaAsP laser diodes
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The large signal dynamic characteristics of partly gain-coupled multiple-quantum-well InGaAsP distributed feedback (GC DFB) laser diodes have been investigated. Simple rate equations for carrier and photon densities were taken. A possibility to simulate the modulation characteristics of GC DFB lasers using these equations has been checked. Chirp and optical power pulses obtained by time-resolved frequency chirp measurements were compared with modeled ones.

articleTitle: A wideband receiver module of the ESM system
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: This work presents a module of the receiver for the 2-18 GHz range, usable in RWR/ESM systems. Details of the construction, principle of operation and technical parameters of the receiver, as a part of the ESM prototype system are given.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of broadband microwave receiver with consideration nonlinear part
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The radioelectronic receiver, from the analysis of the signal to noise point of view, consists of two blocks: linear and nonlinear. Sensitivity of the linear block is generally defined on noise factor or working noise temperature. The influence of the nonlinear receiver's block on the sensitivity of the receiver is rarely considered. Taking into consideration a nonlinear block, especially in broadband receivers (as IFM are) causes significant improvement of sensitivity compared with the obtained sensitivity of the linear block.

articleTitle: Computationally efficient wide-band analysis of transmission line on-platform antennas
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Traditional moment method (MM) schemes are highly demanding in terms of computer memory and execution time required to solve practical problems. Therefore, hybrid approaches combining MM with various approximate techniques have recently received increased attention. This paper proposes an extremely efficient numerical modelling approach based on the well known moment method-physical optics (MM-PO) hybrid formulation combined with the impedance matrix interpolation and adaptive frequency sampling for wide-band analysis of highly resonant transmission line on-platform antennas. Sample numerical results are given for transmission line loop antennas.

articleTitle: Tunable dielectric resonator with circumferentially magnetized ferrite disks
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Electronically tunable dielectric resonator containing circumferentially magnetized ferrite elements has been investigated. The structure of the resonator has been analysed to obtain the optimal parameters. The resonator was constructed whose resonant frequencies can be switched by short current pulses between two stable values that differ in frequency up to 25 MHz with Q-factor value about 4200.

articleTitle: In-line fiber-optic system for depolarization process analysis
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: A detailed theoretical and experimental study of the state of polarization distribution function approach is presented. As a starting point, a theoretical description of this approach is shown, as well as coherence matrix models. Next, the experimental system is introduced, and, based on it, the depolarization process for both models is presented. Experimental results confirming the nonlinear character of the degree of light polarization degradation are shown. The results show that the proposed SOP distribution function approach is more suitable than coherence matrix model for depolarization process investigation. A commercially available semiconductor laser diode operating below the laser action threshold was used in this experiment.

articleTitle: Influence of the dielectric properties of inhomogeneous soil on the dipole antennas' normalized impedance
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: In the paper, a measurement technique for measuring the dielectric permittivity variations in soil is considered. The technique is based on the impedance measurement of a system consisting of two linear dipoles located in parallel to the interface of a flat-layered media. As a result of theoretical and experimental investigations, the main characteristics of the antenna system have been determined. Measurements of layered media were carried out at the test-bench filled by sandy soil. It is demonstrated that the normalized impedance depends on frequency of the sounded signal, geometrical size of the dielectric parameters and depth of the maximum reflecting layer.

articleTitle: Investigations into performances of single layer and stacked configurations of multiband PIFA antenna
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: The paper presents investigations into single layer and stacked configurations of a PIFA terminal antenna for multiband operation. Our findings show that the stacked patch configuration is difficult to tune in individual subbands and the attainable bands are not as broad as for a single layer counterpart. Increasing the operational bandwidth of a single layer PIFA can be achieved by folding and tapering the patch conductor, as well as by careful trimming its coupling to the ground plane.

articleTitle: Some remarks on the design of microstrip to coplanar line transformer
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications (IEEE Cat. No.04EX824)
abstract: Microstrip to coplanar transformer (MS2CPW) with conductor backed coplanar waveguide (CBCPW) design technique is presented. A various structures of the intermediate section layout have been considered. Transformer was developed using Zeland IE3D and Agilent Momentum electromagnetic simulator. Experimental verification and appraisal of electromagnetic simulations allow finding some essential directives to improve design procedure.
